title: Nintendo Switch game store: fan of character-colored cards (low resolution)
contains_third_party_content: Nintendo Switch logo and character art (Mario, Kirby, a Pokemon, Splatoon, Fortnite).

observed.layout: A near-black rounded window on grey. Top bar: Games (active), Store, search, the centered Switch logo, a coin counter, small dots and an avatar. Center text: 'Fun Games Nintendo Switch'. Below: five tilted, overlapping cards, each colored to its character (purple, red, blue-teal center with Kirby, green, yellow-blue). The center card is the largest and highest, with a rating pill (4.7); outer cards tilt and drop. Small floating character icons sit at the corners. The image is 447 px wide, so small text is hard to read.
observed.hierarchy: Headline, then the card fan with its center peak.
observed.typography: Bold sans headline; tiny grey subtitle. Typeface unconfirmed.
observed.materials: Dark ground; vivid per-card color; tilt steps.

interpretation.aesthetic: Dark stage with playful color; each card's color is the game's color.
implementation_notes: Transforms with rotation steps and a scaled center card; carousel logic likely.
interpretation.caveat: Inference; small text could not be verified at this resolution.

concept_work.essence: A fan of cards where each item's own color does the browsing work.
what_makes_it_work: The fan creates a clear focal peak.
Rating pills add a small data layer.
gaps_to_make_it_work: Nav 'Store' measures about 1.93-2.13:1 and the subtitle about 1.52-1.58:1 (small text in a low-resolution image; verify in the source).
The fan hides the lower parts of the cards, including titles.
No hover or selected state beyond the center scale.

links: Card color equals the game's palette.
The center scale marks the current selection.

pattern.name: Fan-of-cards hero
use_when: A small set of items, each with a strong identity color
avoid_when: Items need visible titles or detailed comparison
adaptation_examples: Streaming service: fan of genre cards.
Course platform: fan of tracks colored by subject.

lessons: Do not let a fan hide the card titles.
Use each item's identity color to carry browsing.

measured.palette_method: Median-cut quantization of the supplied image plus saturated-pixel hue medians. Approximate (JPEG). Items marked 'approx' were judged by eye.
measured.color_roles: Near-black ground; each card takes the game's color; the largest card is centered.
measured.contrast_method: Estimated from compressed images. Background = dominant color in a box around the text. ratio_low = conservative estimate (mean of the most distant ~4% of pixels). ratio = best estimate (mean of the most distant ~1.5% of pixels; for text on a saturated background that appears near-white or near-black, the text is assumed pure white or black, because anti-aliasing of small text otherwise understates the contrast). Accessibility scores use ratio_low; critical failure CF1 uses ratio. Gradient or photo backgrounds are measured one text line at a time. Values within 0.4 of a threshold are borderline and should be verified in the source file.

evidence: It reads as a game store landing, but its purpose beyond browsing is unclear.
A clear focal peak and vivid color on a dark stage.
Store/hero conventions are partly met; titles are hidden by overlap.
No hover or selection states beyond the scale.
Cards, tilt and ground are consistent.
The fan device is familiar; the per-card color is well used.
Scored on conservative values: primary text min 1.93:1; secondary text min 1.52:1; icon min n/a:1; non-color state cue: True.
accessibility.basis: computed from measured contrast + cue flag (scope: contrast and non-color cues only; touch targets, motion and screen-reader support cannot be assessed from a static image)

critical_failures.description: A primary text/label measures below 3:1 contrast (best estimate)

evaluation.readiness_key: A = ship with minor adjustments (>=80, no critical failure); B = needs specific fixes (60-79); C = rethink (<60)
evaluation.scope: Scored as presented in a static image. States, motion and behavior that are not shown are not scored as present.
